title: Tenant-protective traffic reshuffle and autoscale guardrail for cross-region latency spikes
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Summary: Prepare and execute a tenant-first traffic reshuffle and autoscale guardrail to mitigate a class of cross-region latency spikes observed in hosted and dedicated fleets. This ticket produces an operational runbook, a small set of emergency automations, and a post-incident checklist tailored for hosted tenants and Dedicated customers who have reserved capacity. Goals: 1) Reduce customer-visible tail latency within 10 minutes of detection for affected regions; 2) Prevent cascading KV cache thundering/evictions during traffic shifts; 3) Protect Premium/Dedicated tenants from noisy neighbors via priority-aware rehome; 4) Provide clear communications and rollback path.
runbook_steps: Detect & verify: On-call receives alert from latency-slo-monitor >3x baseline for region eu-west-1. Confirm spike via latency-dashboard (link below) and sampling of P95/P99 across tenant tiers.

Initial containment (0-5m): Enable regional circuit breaker at routing layer for non-critical traffic by flipping route-weight to reduce new sessions to 30% for best-effort tier. Command: curl -X POST https://routing.internal/api/v1/regions/eu-west-1/weights -d '{"best_effort":0.3,"standard":0.7}' (run from ops jumpbox).
Assess KV cache health: Run kv-metrics query for prefix-hit-rate and eviction-rate. If eviction-rate > 5% and available memory < 20% for >2 nodes, mark as cache-hot and follow Cache-Quarantine step.

Cache-Quarantine (5-12m): For impacted hosts, enable prefix-protect mode to serve resident KV entries and stop aggressive prefetching. Command: python tools/kv_ops.py quarantine --hosts hostlist --mode prefix-protect

Tenant-aware rehome (10-30m): Using the tenant-priority table, shift Premium/Dedicated tenants to warm standby regions with affinity to customer region. Use safe slice approach: create 1% canary rehome, validate response times and output quality, then ramp to 10%, 50%, 100%. CLI: infra rehome --tenants-file tenants.csv --strategy canary --slices 1,10,50,100

Autoscale guardrail (concurrent): Temporarily raise dedicated pool soft-limits for pinned-tenants ONLY and enable conservative burst nodes with preemptible signals turned off. This prevents mass preemption during recovery.

Model fallback & consistency: If model-variant latency is a contributor, fallback affected tenants to a verified lower-latency variant (same model family) and mark fallback in tracing so we can reconcile quality regressions later.

Communication (10-40m): Post incident status to #incidents and pinned customer slack channels: short blurb, affected regions, mitigation actions, ETA for next update. Use template at https://confluence.redwood.ai/pages/CR-comm-template.

Full validation & rollback criteria (30-90m): Monitor P95/P99 and KV hit-rate. If metrics normalize and no new errors for 30 minutes, reverse temporary route weights and drain guard nodes. If regression occurs, reapply quarantine and escalate to senior infra.
Post-incident tasks: Collect traces for rehome windows, export KV snapshots for desync checks, create follow-up ticket for durable fix (e.g., kernel scheduling change or routing policy rewrite).
hosted_vs_dedicated_notes: Hosted: We can perform region-level routing changes and temporary model variant fallbacks globally; users on shared pools may experience broader noise. Prioritize tenant-affinity heuristics to limit blast radius.

Dedicated: Do not perform transparent rehome for Dedicated tenants without consent unless SLA emergency clause is triggered. Use reserved capacity swap tool (infra swap-dedicated) that informs account team and triggers scheduled maintenance window if possible.
Private/VPC: Notify SRE/SE and the customer's on-prem point-of-contact. Provide runbook steps but do not execute customer-side changes without explicit authorization.
safety_and_rollback: All routing changes must be applied using time-limited feature flags with automatic revert after 60 minutes unless explicitly extended by SRE lead.
Store pre-change state with infra snapshot: infra snapshot create --scope region/eu-west-1 --name pre-reshuffle-{{ts}}

Rollback plan: Re-apply previous route weights and rehome back to origin region; warm caches by replaying recent KV snapshots and run low-traffic synthetic warmers for 15 minutes before re-admitting full traffic.
acceptance_criteria: Runbook reviewed and signed off by on-call SRE and PM
Automated guardrail patch (small infra lambda) merged and deployed to staging with e2e smoke tests
Tabletop drill executed with at least 2 on-call rotations and documented run times
Customer communication templates updated and legal/CS informed for Dedicated customers
postmortem_actions: Investigate root cause of cache thundering (kernel scheduling vs prefetching policy)
Ship a model-variant latency certificate for the top 5 heavy tenants to avoid unexpected fallbacks
Add per-tenant warm-standby reservations to Dedicated onboarding checklist
Audit routing policy tests to include KV-stress scenarios
